newsitem.title: GERMANY: Welteke says revaluation row may have hurt Buba.
newsitem.headline: Welteke says revaluation row may have hurt Buba.

text.p: Bundesbank council member Ernst Welteke said on Friday the row over revaluing Germany's official reserves could have hurt the Bundesbank's long term standing.

Speaking at a conference on European economic and monetary union, Welteke said, "I'm afraid that the standing of the German Bundesbank will suffer long term damage", as a result of the dispute over the revaluation of assets.
He said talk of changing the Bundesbank law to force the central bank to make a payout from reserve revaluations was comparable with a central bank making a loan to the state.
Revaluation and a payout in the middle of a financial year would destroy credibility, he added.
Welteke added that an early revaluation of Bundesbank assets was "no longer on the table".
He added Germany could not criticise other nations for wanting to join EMU using special measures if it did so itself.
